demand_narrative.narrative:
Medical Treatment and Pain‑and‑Suffering Narrative

Incident date and initial administrative notes: The emergency‑department record documents a motor‑vehicle collision on March 12, 2026. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 1] Administrative intake records, however, list the incident date as March 13, 2026, and other care‑entry documentation refers to care beginning on March 20, 2026; these differing dates are present in the medical record and are not reconciled in the chart. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 8] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 6] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3]

Initial presentation and emergency‑department care: On March 12, 2026, the emergency department documented that the patient reported neck pain rated 7/10, lower‑back pain rated 6/10, and a headache. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 1] Exam findings included cervical paraspinal tenderness and lumbar paraspinal tenderness. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 1] The ED assessment listed acute cervical strain, acute lumbar strain, and post‑traumatic headache. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 1] Treatment in the ED included administration of acetaminophen, and the patient was discharged with instructions for conservative care and outpatient follow‑up. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 1]

Primary‑care follow‑up: On March 16, 2026, a primary‑care visit documented cervical strain and lumbar strain following the motor‑vehicle collision, and ongoing headaches were noted. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 2]

Physical‑therapy course and conservative management: The patient was referred to Atlanta Rehabilitation & Sports Therapy and was seen by Elena Brooks, DPT, with a documented date of service of March 20, 2026. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3] The initial physical‑therapy evaluation recorded cervical pain 6/10 and lumbar pain 6/10, reduced cervical rotation, and pain with lumbar flexion. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3] Documented physical‑therapy treatments included therapeutic exercise, stretching, manual therapy, postural education, and a home‑exercise program (March 20, 2026). [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3] Subsequent documented PT care (April 3, 2026) included therapeutic exercise, core stabilization, manual therapy, and progression of the home‑exercise program. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 4]

Pain progression and interim functional status during therapy: A progress note dated April 3, 2026 documented that neck pain had improved to 4/10 while low‑back pain remained 5/10 after prolonged sitting. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 4] Functional status at that time included the ability to drive for approximately 30 minutes before needing to change position, and sleep remained interrupted on some nights. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 4]

Diagnostic imaging and orthopedic consultation: A lumbar MRI without contrast performed on April 8, 2026 showed a small posterior L4‑L5 disc protrusion with mild narrowing of the left lateral recess and no acute osseous abnormality. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 5] An orthopedic consultation with Daniel Kim, MD, on April 14, 2026 recorded the assessment of lumbar disc protrusion at L4‑L5 with mechanical low‑back pain and noted an improving cervical strain; the plan was to continue physical therapy and the home‑exercise program and to consider additional intervention only if conservative treatment failed. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 6] The MRI impression and the orthopedic assessment are both documented in the record. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 5] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 6]

Completion of conservative care and discharge from physical therapy: The record documents completion of 12 physical‑therapy visits with discharge to an independent home‑exercise program on May 8, 2026. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7] At discharge, neck symptoms were described as having improved substantially. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7] Low‑back pain was documented as decreased to 2–3/10 with ordinary activity, with occasional discomfort after prolonged sitting. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7] The discharge record also documents that the patient reported sleeping better, completing household activities with fewer breaks, and tolerating longer periods at the computer. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7]

Documented effects on work: The medical record documents that the patient works as a software analyst and reported difficulty remaining seated through normal work periods, with decreased productivity due to frequent position changes and short walking breaks. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 2]

Documented effects on sleep: The chart documents waking during the night because of back discomfort and notes that sleep remained interrupted on some nights during therapy; by discharge the patient reported sleeping better. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 2] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 4] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7]

Documented effects on daily activities and mobility: During the course of care the patient reported needing additional breaks to complete household chores and difficulty lifting laundry baskets. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3] Driving was initially limited to approximately 20 minutes before worsening symptoms were reported, with later documentation that the patient could drive approximately 30 minutes before needing to change position. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 4] By discharge the patient reported completing household activities with fewer breaks and tolerating longer computer periods. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7]

Documented effects on hobbies and recreation: The record documents that the patient stopped recreational basketball, normally played twice weekly, because running and twisting increased back pain; during care the patient had not returned to basketball, and by discharge had begun light shooting drills but had not returned to full games. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 4] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7]

Summary of diagnoses and current plan in the record: Documented diagnoses across the records include acute cervical strain, acute lumbar strain, and post‑traumatic headache on initial ED assessment. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 1] Subsequent primary‑care documentation reiterates cervical strain and lumbar strain. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 2] The MRI and orthopedic assessment document a lumbar disc protrusion at L4‑L5 with mechanical low‑back pain, with the orthopedic plan to continue conservative treatment and consider further intervention only if conservative care fails. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 5] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 6]

This narrative summarizes the documented medical treatment, objective findings, diagnostic imaging, treatment course, and the recorded pain, functional limitations, and effects on work, sleep, daily activities, and recreation as contained in the medical record. [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 1] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 3] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 5] [synthetic_pi_medical_record.pdf, p. 7]
